question: Elite race walkers on a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet burned fat far faster than before. How did their race times change?
options: Improved about as much as others
Did not improve, unlike the others
answer: Did not improve, unlike the others. In Burke's three-week study, fat adaptation raised fat burning to exceptionally high rates, but walking at race pace then cost more oxygen. Walkers eating plenty of carbohydrate cut roughly 5 to 7% from their 10 km times; the fat-adapted group gained nothing.
move: A better number inside the machine is not a faster machine.
ask: Where am I improving an internal number that does not actually make me faster at what matters?
trap: Taking record fat burning as proof of better endurance.
source: Burke et al., Journal of Physiology, 2017
reference: Burke et al., Low carbohydrate, high fat diet impairs exercise economy and negates the performance benefit from intensified training in elite race walkers, Journal of Physiology, 2017
